To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neuromuscular synapse of adult Drosophila undergoes age‐related changes that include morphological alterations, ultrastructural changes, and changes in function.

the neuromuscular synapse of Drosophla melanogaster undergoes age‐dependent changes in its morphology and ultrastructure, which are correlated with changes in endocytosis, membrane dynamics, and synaptic transmission, and that the age‐dependent changes are more pronounced in the temperature‐sensitive shibire mutant, which blocks endocytotic vesicle formation at high temperature.

the neuromuscular (NM) junction of the abdominal dorsal longitudinal muscles in Drosophila undergoes age‐related changes, which include a progressive decrease in branch length and diameter and a progressive increase in the size of synaptic boutons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the neuromuscular synapse in the fruit fly Drosophila.
the study of the neuromuscular system in Drosophila.
the study of the morphology of the NMJ of Drosophla melanogaster throughout adult life, from eclosion until death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aging NMJs in the abdominal muscles of D. melanogaster show morphological and ultrastructural changes that are compatible with a progressive decline in the ability of the nerve terminals to maintain synaptic transmission.

the NMJ of abdominal muscles in the adult D. melanogaster fly shows age‐associated changes, including a progressive increase in bouton size, a progressive decrease in the length of nerve branches, a progressive thinning of the subsynaptic reticular membrane, a progressive decrease of branch diameter, and a progressive increase in autophagy.

the NMJ of the adult Drosophila is a dynamic and functional system, and it can be used as a model for the study not only of synaptogenesis and synaptic function, but also of synaptic plasticity and aging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NMJ in abdominal muscles of adult D. melanogaster undergoes morphological changes during aging, and that the aging‐related alterations in NMJ morphology are associated with a decrease in endocytosis.
the neuromuscular system is a good model for aging studies, and it is a good model because it is simple and well understood, and because the nervous system is a major target of aging.
the neuromuscular synapse of the abdominal muscles of adult Drosophila is a dynamic system that changes with age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aging is a process of gradual deterioration that starts early in adult life, and the neuromuscular system of the adult fly is an excellent system to study this process.
the NMJ of Drosophilamelanogaster undergoes significant structural and functional changes during adult life and aging.
the Drosophila neuromuscular system is a good model system for studying aging and age‐associated changes in the nervous system.
